title: —Elektra review:  @Joe Weinberg  —Kramer/Fauci review:@Joe Weinberg  ...
transcript: The guy who did Sexy Oklahoma on Broadway in 2019 has not one, but two shows coming to New York this fall. And funny enough, I've seen both of them already. So here's the 411 of the two Daniel Fish shows coming this fall, the one that might be a bit more divisive is this revival of Sophocles’ Elektra with a version of the script by the great Anne Carson. When this played in London, it starred Brie Larson and Stockard Channing. I don't think they're gonna come to the New York production, but the cast hasn't been announced yet, so I guess we'll see. And as expected for Daniel Fish, the production is very weird. There's like a machine that shoots ink at all the actors. They're all on microphones. There's like a blimp flying around. There's very eerie choral music composed by Ted Hearne. And this one is playing at Theater for a New Audience from November 10th to December 6th. The second one is called Kramer/Fauci. This one has a script that's taken verbatim from a 1993 TV broadcast with a spirited debate between Anthony Fauci and the playwright Larry Kramer about the AlDS epidemic. And not unlike Elektra, the staging has some very strange theatrical flourishes. It also has Tony Award winner Will Brill. I saw this one when it was playing at Skirball Center this past winter for a very brief run, like only one or two weeks. And now I'm happy to see that It's coming back for a bit of a longer run from September 27th to October 24th at St. Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn. Which, fun fact, is also where Daniel Fish's Oklahoma played before went to Broadway. If you're curious to hear my more detailed thoughts on both of these shows, I linked my reviews in the caption, but generally speaking I would say Kramer/Fauci is the one I feel more comfortable broadly recommending. But if Daniel Fish's style is up your alley, I also think Elektra is worth taking a chance on.
classificationReason: Creator previews two upcoming Daniel Fish NYC productions (Elektra + Kramer/Fauci). While they mention having seen both, the framing is informational/anticipatory about upcoming runs. Elektra is not on the list; Kramer/Fauci is the primary on-list show.
